deliberate_source_vs_oracle_divergence.direction: The encoding is narrower than the oracle. Adopting the oracle's reading would assert exclusion for 39 statistical lines across 10 subheadings that neither note names.

residuals: Membership atoms are held at the precision U.S. notes 50(a)(ii) and 52(b) print them: 8-digit subheadings match the entry's 8-digit rate line, 10-digit statistical reporting numbers match all ten digits. In all twelve cases where either list prints a 10-digit line, it does not also print the enclosing 8-digit subheading, and each named suffix is a substantively distinct article (0409.00.0005 is certified-organic honey; 8505.11.0070 is sintered neodymium-iron-boron magnets; 0712.90.8550, 1204.00.0010, 1205.10.0010, 1205.90.0010 and 1206.00.0031 are the "for sowing" planting-seed lines). Note 52 evidences the intent internally: subdivision (b) lists the 10-digit line where the HTSUS breaks sowing out as a statistical suffix, and subdivision (c) instead lists the 8-digit subheading with the qualifier in prose ("Castor oil seeds, for sowing (classifiable in subheading 1207.30.00)") where it does not. Reading a printed 10-digit atom as naming its whole subheading would assert exclusion for 39 further statistical lines across 10 subheadings that neither list names. An oracle that carves out the whole subheading therefore disagrees with this encoding by design; the divergence is the oracle's coarsening, not an omission here. Enforced by tools/test_b16_entry_flags.py::test_sibling_statistical_suffixes_are_not_carved_out. Measured cost: 120 of the 5,034 Brazil candidate new-disagreement units (2.4%), against 93,192 now-in-scope candidate units; not separately material for note 52.

The general note 6 civil-aircraft lists (50(a)(iv), 52(d)) and the pharmaceutical-use lists (50(a)(v), 52(e)) remain published as conditional tables and are deliberately not netted into either scope flag. Each chapeau is a conjunction that adds a non-panel fact and then says the exclusion applies "regardless of whether a product is entered under a provision for which the rate of duty 'Free (C)'/'Free (K)' appears", so list membership is necessary but not sufficient; the notes are carve-outs from an otherwise-applicable duty, and an exception whose condition is unproven does not apply. This follows the treatment validated main already gives the identically constructed note 2(aa)(iv) list. Measured cost for Brazil, where iso2 == BR is the complete country gate: 228 units (144 GN6, 84 pharmaceutical; 4.6% of the 5,034-unit Brazil candidate set). For note 52 no share is quantified: every note-52 attribution is withdrawn as confounded (oracles_recensus.note52_attribution_history). Enforced by test_conditional_exclusions_do_not_zero_the_scope_flags.

Running in the opposite direction, ten listed lines are over-excluded because an HTS-line key cannot carry an item-level prose qualifier: 50(a)(iii) items (3)(4)(5) are limited to goods "for religious purposes only" (1404.90.90, 1905.90.10, 1905.90.90), and 52(c) items (3)-(7) to seeds "for sowing" (1207.30.00, 1207.40.00, 1207.50.00, 1207.60.00, 1207.99.03) with items (8)(9) "for religious purposes only" (1905.90.10, 1905.90.90). This matches validated main's treatment of the identically worded note 2(aa)(iii) list. Magnitude not measured by the re-census, which censused only the opposite direction; it is bounded by those ten lines.

Only the aluminium and steel part of limb (1) of 50(a)(vi) / 52(f) reaches this lane, through the existing section 232 membership tables. The other limbs - copper, passenger vehicles and their parts, wood products, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and their parts, semiconductor articles, patented pharmaceutical articles - are UNCONSUMED here, not unrepresented in the repository: their sector headings are published as chapter-99 rate cells (us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/lines/generated/ch99c.yaml carries 9903.94.01, 9903.76.01, 9903.74.01 and 9903.79.01 with their own duty columns), and 52(f) additionally has an overlay module, overlays/section-301/forced-labor-metals-9903-05-90.yaml, defining the Asset-level forced_labor_metals_heading_applies. The hand-built CBP composition imports neither, and neither surface is hts_line-keyed, so nothing there carves anything out of a charge in this lane. Receipt v4's 'not represented at all' is withdrawn; the defect is consumption. The Brazil share of the diagnostic candidate set that is not explained by the three joined buckets is bucket E, 4,686 units, a residual with no attribution (oracles_recensus). The note 52 half of this residual as published in receipts v3 and v4 is withdrawn in full: v3 attributed 89.3% of the note-52 candidate set to 52(g)/(h) USMCA and 52(j) as inexpressible (country, HTS line) pairs, and v4 replaced that with a five-way split; both are confounded and no note-52 share is quantified. What the audit established instead, limb by limb: 52(g) Canada and 52(h) Mexico name no article and ARE encoded, as forced_labor_usmca_exception_applies consumed by forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate (entry level only; the panel projection forced_labor_section_301_component_rate that us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate sums never sees them); 52(i), the CAFTA-DR textile and apparel carve-out, enumerates no HTS line and turns on the general note 29(d)(v) definition plus a CAFTA-DR duty-free claim, neither implemented in this composition; 52(j) is thirteen subdivisions, (j)(1)-(j)(13), whose fourteen identifiers (with 52(i)'s article_described_in_heading_9903_05_95) are named across twenty section-301 overlay modules, defined by none, imported by no composition and declared as no entry input - overlay inputs, not gates anyone consumes - and the thirteen per-country annex lists are not implemented; the 52(k) ad valorem equivalent is derived in neither of its two branches. Blocker B3 carries the full statement. Enforced by tools/test_b16_entry_flags.py::test_every_note_52_i_and_j_identifier_is_an_unconsumed_overlay_input and test_note_52_carve_outs_are_encoded_at_entry_level_and_absent_from_the_total.

Residual, open and undischarged - U.S. note 50 / heading 9903.05.01 Brazil additional duty. Three exceptions to that duty are applied nowhere TO THAT DUTY; the scope of the statement is the Brazil charge, not the repository. Two of the three underlying facts exist and are consumed elsewhere: entry_is_humanitarian_donation_article and entry_is_informational_material_article are declared composition inputs read by the IEEPA fentanyl exception rules (composition.yaml 2407, 2436, 2470-2471) and by forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate (3799-3800). Zero Brazil rules read them. The third, the heading 9903.05.02 July 22 in-transit window, is absent outright: no declared entry input states it, and the only in-transit input, entry_loaded_and_in_transit_before_july_24_2026, is note 52's July 24 window. The three exceptions: the heading 9903.05.02 in-transit window, the heading 9903.05.08 donation exception, and the heading 9903.05.09 informational-material exception. All three appear in us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/lines/generated/ch99c.yaml only as rate columns - "Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading", that is, without heading 9903.05.01's "+ 25%" - and no rule selects those headings for an entry. The entry-level charge is "if entry_is_brazil_301_listed and origin_is_brazil: brazil_section_301_additional_duty_rate else: 0"; COMPONENT_RULES contains no brazil_section_301_entry_component_rate, and DECLARED_BOOLEAN_INPUTS declares no fact for the heading 9903.05.02 window - its only in-transit input, entry_loaded_and_in_transit_before_july_24_2026, is note 52's July 24 window. The overlay module overlays/section-301/brazil-9903-05-01.yaml names article_described_in_headings_9903_05_02_through_9903_05_09, negated inside its Asset-level heading_applies rule. No module defines that identifier, so it is an overlay INPUT rather than a derivation; the composition imports that module only for brazil_section_301_additional_duty_rate, references neither heading_applies nor the identifier anywhere (grep for 'article_described' and 'heading_applies' in composition.yaml returns zero hits), and declares neither as an entry input. Consequence: an entry qualifying for any of the three is over-charged the full heading 9903.05.01 additional duty. Note 52's analogous exceptions (heading 9903.05.85 in-transit, headings 9903.05.91 and 9903.05.92) are by contrast applied by forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate, the entry-level rule for that family (not 'legally complete' as to note 52, whatever the composition's own wording says: it carries neither 52(a)'s reduced bases, nor 52(i), nor any of the thirteen limbs of 52(j), nor the 52(k) equivalent), which note 50 has no counterpart to - though that rule is itself not consumed by us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate, which takes the non-exempt projection forced_labor_section_301_component_rate. Enforced by tools/test_b16_entry_flags.py::test_note_50_transaction_fact_residual_is_still_open. This residual was omitted from receipt v2 and is restored here.

Residual, open and newly declared - the U.S. note 50(a)(i) and U.S. note 52(a) reduced duty bases. Both notes except 9802.00.40, 9802.00.50, 9802.00.60 and 9802.00.80 entries from their chapter 98 exclusion and then prescribe a reduced base for them rather than the full charge: 'the additional dut[y/ies] appl[ies/y] to the value of repairs, alterations or processing performed, as described in the applicable subheading' for the three subheadings, and 'the value of the article assembled abroad, less the cost or value of such products of the United States' for 9802.00.80. No rule in this repository states either base for either note. For note 52 the consequence is exact: entry_is_9802_excepted_entry turns forced_labor_chapter_98_exclusion_applies off, so the excepted entry falls through to forced_labor_section_301_component_rate, an ad valorem rate on FULL customs value, overstating the duty. For note 50 there is no entry-level rule at all - no brazil_section_301_entry_component_rate - so the accompanied-baggage exclusion, the whole chapter 98 exclusion and all four bases are unapplied, and qualifying entries are over-charged. The contrast that makes this a gap rather than a convention is in the same composition: U.S. note 51(a) prescribes the identical bases for section 338 and they ARE encoded, as section_338_reduced_duty_base_applies (proof atoms quoting both sentences) exposed by section_338_entry_component_rate. The same pattern appears in this lane's own generator, which emits 9802 partial-value-share rules for the China 301 and section 122 families and none for notes 50 or 52. Note 50 is NOT entry-complete and note 52's entry rule is not complete as to 52(a). Enforced by tools/test_b16_entry_flags.py::test_no_rule_applies_a_note_50_or_note_52_reduced_duty_base.

blockers.title: U.S. note 52 is applied in part only: 52(g)/(h) entry level only, 52(i) and all thirteen limbs of 52(j) consumed by nothing, both 52(k) AVE branches absent, and 52(a)'s four 9802 reduced bases absent
blockers.detail: Corrects receipt v3 (which treated 52(g)-(j) as inexpressible country+HTS pairs) and narrows receipt v4 (which described 52(j) as the United Kingdom and European Union lists). 52(g) Canada and 52(h) Mexico name no article and ARE encoded: forced_labor_usmca_exception_applies, consumed by forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate, which the panel total does not sum. 52(a)'s chapter 98 and accompanied-baggage exclusions are likewise encoded at entry level only - but 52(a) also prescribes reduced duty bases for 9802.00.40/.50/.60/.80 entries and NO rule states them, so an excepted 9802 entry falls through to an ad valorem rate on full customs value. 52(i) is the CAFTA-DR textile and apparel carve-out, turning on the general note 29(d)(v) definition, origin in the six parties, and entry free of duty under CAFTA-DR including subchapter XXII of chapter 98; it enumerates no HTS line. 52(j) is thirteen subdivisions, (j)(1) through (j)(13) - United Kingdom, European Union, Switzerland, Malaysia, Cambodia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Argentina, Bangladesh, Taiwan, Indonesia, Ecuador, Jordan - carried by headings 9903.05.96, 9903.05.97, 9903.05.98 and 9903.05.99 through 9903.06.21, each naming HTSUS provisions country by country. Fourteen identifiers for 52(i)+52(j) are named across twenty section-301 overlay modules; no module DEFINES any of them, so each is an overlay input, and the composition imports none of those modules, references none of the fourteen and declares none as an entry input. 52(k) is split: the tier ceiling arithmetic is on the panel path, but the ad valorem equivalent is derived in neither of its two branches - not the column 1-General branch for goods of the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland or Taiwan, and not the separate South Korea column 1-Special branch.
blockers.consequence: UNQUANTIFIED. Every quantified note-52 attribution is withdrawn (see oracles_recensus.note52_attribution_history). Separately, 52(g)/(h), 52(a)'s chapter 98 and baggage exclusions and the heading 9903.05.85/.91/.92 exceptions are applied only on forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate, which us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate does not consume, so no panel-facing result reflects any of them.
blockers.discharged_by: A country-qualified table alone discharges NONE of this. 52(i) needs a declared general note 29(d)(v) textile/apparel fact AND a declared CAFTA-DR duty-free claim AND a composition rule consuming them. 52(j) needs extraction of all thirteen per-country annex lists AND a (country, article) table kind AND consumption. 52(k) needs an ad valorem equivalent derivation for specific and compound rates, in both branches. 52(a)'s reduced bases need a reduced-base rule of the section_338_reduced_duty_base_applies shape for note 52 (and its twin for note 50). None of these is 52(g) or 52(h).
blockers.not_claimed: The composition's own summary calls forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate the 'legally complete' CustomsEntry rate for this family (composition.yaml lines 562, 588, 592 and the rule's source line). That wording is pre-existing and false on the facts above. This lane does not repeat it, does not rely on it, and did not edit composition.yaml.
